173911.evidence: Every handler passes request.user.orgId to credentialVaultService/connector service; repository filters by organization_id (credential-vault.repository.ts:30-78 findFirst where {id, organization_id}). Vault routes carry authenticate/requireModifyAccess. Named control verified on all routes.

d8b251.evidence: All handlers pass request.user.orgId into apiKeyService.revokeApiKey/deleteApiKey (org-scoped where) and mcpServerService.getMcpServerById(id, orgId); mcp.repository findAll filters by organizationId. Auth + requireModifyAccess present on all mutating routes.

1c6035.evidence: Handlers pass request.user.orgId into repositories/services which filter by organization_id (chat.repository findById where {id, organization_id}; document.service getDocumentById(id, orgId)); agents routes use orgId in where clauses. Same-org user-level (non-org) sharing is by design, not cross-tenant.

d22150.risk_area: Agent tool execution approval boundary — unapproved Bash/host command execution
d22150.evidence: Real buildOptions() instantiated locally with repo .env: permissionMode=bypassPermissions, allowDangerouslySkipPermissions=true, allowedTools incl. Bash/Write/Edit/WebFetch. Only gate is PreToolUse regex denylist (claude-hooks.ts), proven bypassable locally (python3 -c marker written to /tmp after hook returned allow).

f4cd86.risk_area: IDOR / cross-tenant data access via RAG retrieval
f4cd86.evidence: GET /api/rag/search and POST /api/rag/index/:fileId have only authenticate (no requireModifyAccess, no org scoping). ragRetrieverService.retrieve/retrieveByKnowledgeBases (rag-retriever.service.ts:62-80) filter only by knowledge_base_id/document_group_id with no organization_id anywhere in the chain; documentIndexerService.indexFile takes orgId but knowledge-base scoping is absent on the retrieve paths. Cross-org document-chunk content disclosure if foreign KB IDs are supplied. Partially covered by the KB IDOR family (vuln-0001); retrieve-by-KB-IDs path is a distinct unscoped query chain.

9cd308.risk_area: Agent tool execution approval boundary — unrestricted tool execution in container
9cd308.evidence: Static trace: hardcoded permissionMode bypassPermissions + allowDangerouslySkipPermissions, DEFAULT_TOOLS incl Bash/Write/WebSearch; the only hooks registered are PostToolUse S3-sync and Stop — no PreToolUse security hook at all, so any tool call (incl. from injected prompt content) executes without approval or filtering.

5c192a.evidence: Confirmed cross-org IDOR: knowledgeBaseService queries by bare ID with no organization scoping (findById line 69, update 80, delete 91, folder ops 190-218); briefing routes filter only business_scope_id. Local PoC tests pass (vuln-0001, vuln-0002).

ec7d29.surface: claude-hooks.ts dangerousCommandBlocker / PATH_ESCAPE_PATTERNS / file_path prefix check
ec7d29.evidence: Imported real hook code and tested: python3 -c, node -e, $HOME writes pass the Bash denylist; Write file_path check uses un-normalized startsWith(cwd) so cwd/../../etc/shadow passes; ../../etc is caught only because it matches '..' regex, not by canonicalization.

40bd6c.surface: Remaining backend route files (scope-memory, rehearsal, integrations, projects, workflows, tasks, skills, enterprise-skills, showcase, pack-deploy, token-usage, schedules, webhooks, checkpoint, userGroups, document-groups, support, im admin, organizations, businessScopes, scope-generator, chat, execution, agentPermissions, audit, litellm, apps, appData, appBackend, a2a, openapi, widget, im webhooks)
40bd6c.evidence: Substantially resolved by follow-up sweep: projects, workflows, tasks, scope-memory, rehearsal, integrations, skills, enterprise-skills, showcase, checkpoint, pack-deploy, appData, appBackend, im, apps, organizations, avatarRoutes verified org-scoped (entry b09954); userGroups, scopeMemberships, businessScopes plugin/MCP, support group routes confirmed vulnerable and reported (vuln-0008..0011). Still only spot-checked (not per-handler verified): a2a, openapi, llm-proxy, widget, token-usage, schedules, webhooks, audit, agentPermissions, chat-session, execution, scope-generator, im admin, document-groups — all authenticate and use API-key/signature auth, but handler-level org scoping unverified.

history.evidence: Bounded scan: every file uses authenticate on protected routes (counted preHandler refs vs route counts); a2a/openapi/llm-proxy/widget use hashed API-key auth; im webhooks verify provider signatures. However per-handler org-scoping was only spot-checked for the priority files, not exhaustively verified for all 30+ remaining files. RAG retrieve path left as reported gap entry f4cd86. Deep per-handler verification of the remaining route files is unfinished.

6a4fe2.risk_area: Shell command injection in container command wrappers
6a4fe2.evidence: Reviewed sanitizePath (rejects .., leading /, backtick $ ; | & < >) and shellEscape ($'...' with backslash and single-quote escaping); heredoc writer uses quoted delimiter. No injected-path route found; wrappers build fixed commands with sanitized relative paths only. Reachability requires an already-authenticated chat session (AGENT_RUNTIME=agentcore), consistent with design.

55aebc.surface: RAG / knowledge / retrieved-content flow into agent prompt (backend + agentcore container)
55aebc.risk_area: Indirect prompt injection reaching tool execution boundary
55aebc.evidence: Traced: container gets AUTH_TOKEN to call backend RAG search; workspace skills/SKILL.md are restored from S3 into the prompt context; user message flows verbatim as prompt. Injection reachability at the LLM layer is stochastic and cannot be validated locally without a live model — but the *consequence* boundary (unapproved tool execution) is separately confirmed as broken (see the two reported surfaces). No egress filtering on WebFetch/WebSearch exists in agentcore runtime.
